description: Standard basketball starting formations (offense and zone defense), expressed via FIBA named positions so they resolve correctly across rulesets.

5_out.title: 5 Out
5_out.description: All five offensive players positioned beyond the three-point line — including bigs who can shoot. Keeps the area under the basket completely open for drives and cuts.

4_out_1_in.title: 4 Out, 1 In
4_out_1_in.description: Four players spaced along the three-point line, one post player (usually the center) directly at the basket. The most commonly used modern formation — spacing for shooters plus a post/roll threat.

3_out_2_in.title: 3 Out, 2 In
3_out_2_in.description: Three perimeter players and two post players. A classic, physical system where two bigs control the area under the basket for rebounds and close-range scoring.

horns.title: Horns
horns.description: Point guard with the ball up top; two bigs at the high post/elbows, two perimeter players in the corners. The layout resembles a bull's horns — a strong starting shape for quick ball-screen actions (pick and roll).

princeton.title: Princeton
princeton.description: Backdoor-cut-heavy motion offense built around high-post ball distribution. Starting shape has a big at the high post as a passing hub, with perimeter players spaced to read backdoor cuts.

1_4_low.title: 1-4 Low
1_4_low.description: One ball handler up top, four players in a line along the baseline/blocks area. Common for baseline out-of-bounds plays and staggered-screen actions.

1_4_high.title: 1-4 High
1_4_high.description: One ball handler up top, four players spaced along the elbow/free-throw-line-extended area. Common starting shape for double-screen and dribble-handoff actions.

zone_2_3.title: 2-3 Zone Defense
zone_2_3.description: Two defenders up top at the three-point line, three defenders across the baseline near the basket. Protects the paint but is vulnerable against good three-point shooting.

zone_3_2.title: 3-2 Zone Defense
zone_3_2.description: Three defenders up top, two defenders back near the basket. Pressures perimeter shooters but leaves the corners more open.

zone_1_3_1.title: 1-3-1 Zone Defense
zone_1_3_1.description: One defender up top, three across the middle, one at the baseline. An aggressive variant meant to block passes into the middle and force turnovers.
